Michael Cloud

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 27, Travis County, Texas · Incumbent

U.S. Representative for Texas's 27th Congressional District (incumbent)

Michael Cloud is the Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 27th Congressional District and has held the seat since winning a special election in July 2018. He won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 73.0% of the vote against Chris Hatley. He faces Democrat Tanya Lloyd in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Cloud stands

Public Education
Supports less federal oversight of education. Says teachers should be freed to teach and parents should have more say in their children's educational choices.
Healthcare
Supports repealing the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare). Supports a market-based approach that he says would lower costs and expand access to quality care.
Economy & Federal Spending
Supports federal spending cuts to address the national debt, fewer federal regulations, and a simpler tax code. Signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge.
Abortion
Opposes abortion and opposes taxpayer funding for abortion. Endorsed by Texas Alliance for Life and Texas Right to Life PAC.
Agriculture & Rural Issues
Opposes EPA and other federal regulations that he says interfere with the property rights of farmers and ranchers.
Energy & Environment
Supports more domestic oil, natural gas, and coal production to reach energy independence. Voted for the Lower Energy Costs Act (H.R. 1).
Democracy & Elections
Voted against certifying the 2020 electoral votes from Arizona and Pennsylvania. Voted for the SAVE Act (H.R. 22), which requires proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.
Immigration & Border Security
Says immigration reform should begin with securing the border. Voted for the Laken Riley Act and for H.R. 875, which makes DUIs deportable offenses.
Gun Policy
Supports Second Amendment gun rights and opposes federal restrictions on lawful gun ownership.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Texas's 27th District, July 2018–present (won 2018 special election; succeeded Blake Farenthold)
  • Member, House Appropriations Committee; member, House Freedom Caucus
  • Won 2026 Republican primary for TX-27 with 73.0% (44,159 votes)
  • Education: B.S., Oral Roberts University
  • Born May 13, 1975, in Baton Rouge, Louisiana
